name: gnfs_relation_collection_circuit

phase_0.boundary_condition: The integer N and its base-m polynomial representation: monic f(x)=x^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+...+a_0 with 0<=a_i<m and f(m)=N, together with g(x)=x-m. m is the junction where g(m)=0 and f(m)=N=0 mod N; the factor base of small primes bounds smoothness on each arm.

⊢.justification: the void state before factorization; N exists but no relations or field structure are established

⊣.justification: the terminal anchor where the product of the found factors equals N, closing the system

≻.justification: forward morphism selecting monic f with f(m)=N and g(x)=x-m, mapping N into the number fields

≺.justification: reverse morphism descending from the algebraic relation back to the integer domain to pull out a factor

⋈.justification: composition chaining individual smooth relations into the sparse matrix over GF(2)

⊙.justification: identity self-reference; the set of primes fixing the smoothness threshold stays invariant

∈.justification: splits the candidate (a,b) into the rational arm a-bm and the algebraic arm F(a,b)=b^d f(a/b)

∋.justification: reconstitutes the candidate relation (a,b) from the two arms; the joint smoothness is held at B

⊤.justification: affirmative channel: a-bm factors completely over the rational factor base

⊥.justification: negative-orientation channel: F(a,b) factors completely over the algebraic factor base

⊞.justification: both arms simultaneously smooth, held at B without Boolean retraction

⊡.justification: permanent, append-only record of the retained relation (a,b)

phase_2.split_input: Candidate relation (a,b) carrying the shared divisor m
phase_2.fuse_result: Candidate relation (a,b) carrying the shared divisor m
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: no relations collected; the relation matrix is empty (00)
phase_3.true_description: the rational side is smooth, a relation is partially established (01)
phase_3.false_description: only the algebraic side is smooth; the candidate fails the rational test (10)
phase_3.both_description: BOTH sides are smooth — a valid relation held at B before Boolean retraction (11)

steps.domain_action: initialize the system with the target integer N to be factored
define the Factor Base, the invariant set of small primes used for smoothness testing
select the base-m polynomials f(x)=x^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+...+a_0 (monic, f(m)=N) and g(x)=x-m
branch the candidate (a,b) into the rational arm and the algebraic arm
evaluate the rational arm a-bm and deposit T when it is smooth over the factor base
evaluate the algebraic arm F(a,b)=b^d f(a/b) and deposit F when it is smooth over the algebraic factor base
rejoin the two arms into the candidate relation (a,b), holding the joint verdict B when both are smooth
hold the paradice relation — rational and algebraic smoothness simultaneously, without Boolean retraction
record the retained relation (a,b) permanently in the relation log
aggregate the retained relations into the sparse matrix over GF(2)
branch the linear algebra phase into the rational and algebraic square-root searches
identify a subset of relations whose product forms a square on the rational side
identify a subset of relations whose product forms a square on the algebraic side
rejoin the two square roots into a single dependency vector
compute the GCD of the square-root difference against N to descend to a factor
verify the factor divides N, closing the factorization process

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Polynomial selection translating N into its compact base-m algebraic structure and two number fields
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: relation vectors passed between sieving workers and the central matrix builder
phase_5.memory_mechanism: sparse matrix storing exponents of the factor-base primes modulo 2
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the lattice sieving grid that determines the order of candidate evaluation
phase_5.alfs_store: the set of all smooth numbers over the factor base within the sieving range

phase_6.cycle_cost: the work to test smoothness on both arms and solve the linear system
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: integer N with no known factors
phase_6.post_cycle_state: integer N decomposed into factors p and q
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information content of N is conserved; factorization reveals hidden structure without creating or destroying the integer's value
